title: Reconstruct a responsive service operations dashboard in Leptos
objective: Implement a complete, visually coherent, responsive Leptos CSR page from an original product brief and a held-back browser-rendered reference fixture. The page must preserve the information hierarchy, semantic regions and usability across desktop, tablet and mobile.

users: Technician reviewing team activity and today's schedule
product_brief.user_goal: Understand current operational workload, recent activity and upcoming appointments at a glance.

visual_direction.mood: Calm, trustworthy, organic and professional; a restrained solarpunk operations product rather than a generic admin template.
visual_direction.typography: Use a native system sans-serif stack; distinct heading hierarchy, compact but readable metadata, tabular numeric values.
layout_principles: Desktop uses a 76px header, a 236px workspace sidebar and a fluid main content region.
The main content has a three-column metric row and a two-column activity/schedule region.
Surfaces use subtle borders, modest radii and restrained shadows rather than heavy glass effects.
At tablet and mobile widths, navigation and workspace regions reflow without hiding required information.
At narrow mobile widths, metric cards stack into one column and the primary action remains full-width.

interaction_requirements: Primary and workspace navigation links move to their corresponding page sections.
The create-work-order action has a visible, reachable destination anchor; creating or submitting a work order is outside this static task.
A skip-to-main-content link is available and becomes visible on keyboard focus.

allowed_dependencies: Existing Leptos dependencies already present in the selected starter application
disallowed_techniques: No React, Vue, Angular, Svelte or JavaScript UI framework.
No CDN scripts, remote fonts, remote images or runtime network dependencies.
No screenshot hardcoding, canvas painting or one giant embedded screenshot as a substitute for semantic UI.
No use of aria-label to paper over incorrect native semantics when visible text or a native label is appropriate.
Do not weaken browser, accessibility or test gates.

environment.browser: Headless Chromium; exact browser build must be recorded by the runner before the task can become runnable.
environment.network_policy: Fixture-only origin; deny external requests. Use an isolated disposable browser/network namespace. Do not expose host CDP or allow arbitrary private-network access.
environment.font_policy: Use only fonts installed in the pinned runner image; no remote font requests.

reference_fixture.purpose: Original static HTML/CSS reference fixture. The digest is SHA-256 over UTF-8 bytes of reference.html, one NUL byte, then UTF-8 bytes of style.css. Do not expose fixture source to the evaluated agent when the benchmark is run in screenshot-conditioned mode.

acceptance_journeys.goal: Reach primary page navigation and content using keyboard only.
steps: Press Tab from the document start.
Observe and activate the skip link.
Continue through navigation and the primary action.
oracle: The skip link becomes visible on focus and moves focus to main content.
All visible navigation links and the create-work-order action are keyboard operable.
Focus indication is visible and not obscured.

acceptance_journeys.goal: Preserve hierarchy and operability as the viewport narrows.
steps: Sweep widths from 320px to 1440px in 37px increments.
Record document overflow and all required source-region bounding boxes.
oracle: No horizontal document overflow at any sampled width.
Required regions remain present and visible.
Metric cards reflow from three columns to one column at narrow widths.
The create-work-order action remains visible and operable.

assertions.rationale: The interface must have one unambiguous main landmark.
The three metric cards must be independently identifiable in the implementation.
Desktop metric cards should form three columns.
Metric cards should stack at narrow mobile width.

assertions.target: visual hierarchy and alignment across desktop/tablet/mobile
assertions.rationale: A blinded reviewer checks hierarchy, spacing, visual rhythm and information density.

assertions.target: operability and readability at all reference widths

hard_gates: No horizontal document overflow at any fixed or swept viewport.
Exactly one main landmark and one level-one page heading with the required accessible name.
All eight required regions are present and visible.
No external script, font or image requests.
Keyboard-only navigation works and the skip link is visible on focus.
No critical accessibility issue or keyboard trap.
evidence: Source commit and dependency lock digest.
Pinned Chromium build, OS image, installed font manifest and viewport list.
One content-addressed screenshot per fixed viewport.
Frontend layout evidence receipt including the eight required regions.
Keyboard navigation trace and human review record.
notes: Fixture assets are original and contain no remote resources.
The fixture source is the visual reference; screenshot-conditioned evaluations should provide screenshots and the product brief, not the fixture HTML/CSS.
This task is not yet runnable: an isolated fixture server, exact browser pin, screenshot baseline and independent oracle implementation remain pending.

The reference fixture labels dashboard heading, activity and schedule regions with aria-labelledby, and labels the workspace complementary landmark. Three metric cards carry unique dashboard.metric-card.* source anchors for layout assertions.
